Let me think about this year's planting.

I have 8.5 mu. Like every year, I put winter wheat on all of it, and after the wheat comes off in June, I plant sunflower on the bigger piece and some maize on the smaller piece. Sunflower is what I know best — most of us in the village grow it. I keep about 5.5 mu for sunflower and 3 mu for maize, same as last year. It worked, so I do the same.

For the wheat, last autumn I already put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's what the dealer sells us, and my neighbor Old Wang does the same. In spring when the wheat turns green I will spread urea, about one bag (40 kg) for every two mu. If the leaves still look yellow I add a little more. I would rather put a handful too much than watch the wheat go thin — that would be a disaster. I will water the wheat maybe three or four times from the well — once when it greens up, once at jointing, once at heading, and once when the grain fills if the sky stays dry. I spray twice: once for weeds in spring, once for aphids before heading.

For the sunflower, I don't put much fertilizer — sunflower does not need as much as maize, everyone says so. One bag of compound before planting and maybe half a bag of urea when it is knee-high. I water it once or twice, because sunflower stands the dry better. I spray once for the worms that eat the head, otherwise the seeds come out empty.

For the maize, I put one bag of compound in the furrow when planting, then urea at the big trumpet stage, about one bag for every mu and a half. Maize eats a lot. I water twice — once after planting if no rain, once at tasseling. I spray once for the borer.

I use the small rotary tiller the village machine does — everyone uses it, it is cheap and fast. Seeds I buy the improved kind from the same shop as last year; the wheat variety gave me over 450 kg last year so I will stick with it. My son helps at harvest, otherwise it is me.
